newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovene Digitel to invest some $60 mln in 10 years.
newsitem.headline: Slovene Digitel to invest some $60 mln in 10 years.

text.p: Slovenian unlisted mobile phone operator Digitel said on Thursday it planned to invest about $60 million over the next 10 years to establish a mobile phone network.
"The total amount of investment will be approximately $60 million over 10 years," Boris Milevoj, a member of the company's managing board, told a news conferenece.

The company said it expected to receive permission from the state to use radio frequencies for mobile phone operations on Friday. Currently only state-owned Mobitel has a licence to use radio frequencies.
Last week the Constitutional Court ruled that Mobitel's telephone network monopoly was unconstitutional and said that other firms must be given licences on equal grounds.
Digitel said it would start to construct a network in September which would cover Slovenia's northern region of Gorenjska and be fully operational by the end of the first quarter of next year.
"Around the beginning of the next millenium there will be some 200,000 mobile phone users. If we get a stake of 45,000 our investment will return over the long-term," Milevoj said.
Currently there are 59,500 mobile phone users in Slovenia.
So far three companies -- Digitel, Detel 5 and Si.Mobil, which was established by consortium GSM -- have said they would like to operate in the Slovenian mobile telecommunications sector.
